abstract: With the increasing availability of large datasets and the growing importance of artificial intelligence (AI), robust and sustainable data management systems have become essential for plant and ecosystem research. In particular, the integration of heterogeneous spectral data with plant functional traits and environmental measurements from multiple sensors poses a major challenge, requiring significant time investment and long-term planning. Here, we present SPECTRE (Spectral, Trait, and Remote-sensing Ecophysiology data framework), a versatile data framework based on simple, open data formats that addresses the need of many research groups for a standardized organization of heterogeneous datasets, facilitating their integration and joint analysis without relying on proprietary software or external service providers. SPECTRE integrates a wide range of datasets linking spectral measurements to plant traits, including LiDAR, hyperspectral imagery, chlorophyll fluorescence, geospatial data, soil moisture, climate variables, and ecophysiological traits, organized into three main categories: (i) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-acquired data, (ii) ground-based trait measurements, and (iii) environmental data. All datasets are stored using a standardized folder structure and converted to comma-separated values (CSV) format. A unified primary key enables consistent linking of spectral signatures to functional traits across datasets by species and site, facilitating trait-based analyses, data framework extension, and long-term usability. The widespread use of lookup tables reduces data redundancy and facilitates the integration of data with different naming conventions, while the use of Markdown for metadata and documentation ensures easy access to information without relying on complex or proprietary formats, simplifying documentation creation and maintenance. Overall, SPECTRE offers a simple, transparent, and scalable solution that can be readily adopted by plant ecophysiological laboratories, facilitating future AI-driven trait prediction analyses.
